Stories & credits

These short, child-friendly retellings introduce Hindu devotional traditions. Stories and customs vary across regions and families. The nine forms are presented in the Navadurga sequence, ending with Siddhidatri.

  • Navaratri — festival, Navadurga, and regional practices
  • The Divine India — The Story of Navratri
  • Tell-A-Tale — goddess stories and linked individual retellings
  • Aana Avanna — Navarathri and Tamil household traditions
  • Golu — dolls, home visits, music, and puja customs

The later slides focus on customs familiar in many Tamil Brahmin (TamBram) homes. These are shared with wider Tamil Hindu communities. Iyer, Iyengar, and individual household practices vary; the slideshow describes examples rather than a single ritual rulebook.

The children’s drawing and six-second battle animation were supplied by the host and are credited to our young storytellers. They are shown as the children’s artistic retelling.

LEGO-style goddess illustrations supplied by the host. LE’Golu is a family celebration theme, with no claim of LEGO endorsement.

Background music: Aigiri Nandini (Mahishasura Mardini), a Revathi flute-and-keyboard arrangement supplied by the host as Aigiri_Nandini_Revathi_Flute_Keyboard.mid.
